reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Circuit court application for incorporation on assessment plan
headings.reviewNote: Seven or more Missouri citizens may apply to circuit court with articles setting forth objects, methods, and plans.

headings.title: Recording of court decree and state filing
headings.reviewNote: Applicant must record certified articles and decree with county recorder of deeds and file with secretary of state.

headings.title: Charter issuance, name approval, policyholder minimums, and deposit
headings.reviewNote: Secretary of state issues charter after director certifies distinct name, 100+ applicants for $100,000+ insurance, and $30,000 beneficiary fund deposit; defines casualty insurance.

headings.title: Prohibition on new assessment incorporations after 1953
headings.reviewNote: Bars incorporation of new assessment plan companies after September 1, 1953, preserving rights of existing licensed companies.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939–1953); tightened subsections 2 and 4 titles; assessment incorporation, casualty definition, and post-September 1, 1953 bar on new assessment incorporations verified.

headings.title: Application for release of beneficiary trust funds
headings.reviewNote: Board of directors applies in writing to director to release beneficiary funds for paying policy beneficiaries.

headings.title: Board certification of beneficiary claims
headings.reviewNote: Board certifies beneficiary names and claim amounts, swearing funds will be used solely to pay certified claims.

headings.title: Twelve thousand dollar limit on released funds
headings.reviewNote: Released amount cannot exceed twelve thousand dollars and must be used solely to pay beneficiaries.

headings.title: Quarterly replacement of released funds within twelve months
headings.reviewNote: Company must replace released funds within twelve months in four equal installments, subject to director extension.

headings.title: Inapplicability to certain existing companies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts previously incorporated Missouri companies from §§ 377.020–377.030 and preserves authority to combine life and casualty clauses in one policy.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; beneficiary trust release up to $12,000, quarterly replacement, and existing-company exemption verified.

headings.title: Declaration for reincorporation or assessment plan authorization
headings.reviewNote: Domestic company with 500+ members and $500,000+ insurance may file declaration, charter, bylaws, and one assessment in bank.

headings.title: Director certificate authorizing transaction of business
headings.reviewNote: Director issues certificate permitting business under department supervision upon full compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; 500-member/$500,000 declaration and director certificate for assessment plan authorization verified.

headings.title: Accumulation and investment of trust emergency fund
headings.reviewNote: Life companies accumulate one death assessment, casualty companies maximum policy, within six months; invested in legal securities.

headings.title: Deposit of emergency securities and exchange rights
headings.reviewNote: Securities deposited in trust with director, with company retaining right to exchange for equivalent securities.

headings.title: Requisition to draw securities during excess mortality
headings.reviewNote: Requisition by two-thirds of directors permitted if six-month death rate exceeds American life tables mortality rate.

headings.title: Six-month deficiency replenishment and joint credit safe deposit
headings.reviewNote: Company must replace deficiency within six months; securities held in St. Louis safe deposit to joint credit.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; tightened subsection 2 title; emergency fund accumulation, St. Louis joint-credit safe deposit, excess mortality requisition, and 6-month replenishment verified.

headings.title: Age limits, insurable interest requirement, and payment calls
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits policies on persons over sixty, without insurable interest, or living endowments; payment calls must state purpose.

headings.title: Invalidity of policy assignments lacking insurable interest
headings.reviewNote: Assignment of policy or certificate to person lacking insurable interest in insured life is void and of no effect.

headings.title: Insurable interest of qualified charitable organizations
headings.reviewNote: Section 501(c)(3) entities deemed to have insurable interest upon beneficiary designation, gift, or consent under section 376.531.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939–1997); age-60 limit, void assignment without insurable interest, and 501(c)(3) insurable interest under § 376.531 verified.

headings.title: Board vote and filings for regular life reincorporation
headings.reviewNote: Assessment company board may vote to accept sections 376.010 to 376.670, amend articles with attorney general approval, and deposit securities.

headings.title: Rights and privileges of reincorporated regular life company
headings.reviewNote: Reincorporated company exercises all rights and privileges of companies originally formed under chapter 376.

headings.title: Continuity of existing contracts and prospective statutory construction
headings.reviewNote: Existing contracts continue in force; subsequent contracts construed under chapter 376.

headings.title: Preservation of pending actions and previously acquired rights
headings.reviewNote: Compliance does not prejudice, impede, or impair pending proceedings or previously acquired rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; board reincorporation under §§ 376.010–376.670 and preservation of existing contracts and pending actions verified.

headings.title: Articles of agreement for stipulated premium life company
headings.reviewNote: Corporators execute articles detailing name, office, minimum $50,000 capital and $50,000 surplus, board, duration, and 1963–1965 $25,000 capital grandfathering.

headings.title: Approval of articles by director and attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Articles submitted to director and attorney general for approval of statutory compliance.

headings.title: Filing and issuance of certificate of incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Approved articles filed with secretary of state, who issues certificate creating body corporate and politic.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939, 1963); tightened subsection 3 title; stipulated premium articles, $50,000 capital/surplus with 1963–1965 $25,000 grandfathering, and approvals verified.

headings.title: Subscription minimums, premium trust, and security deposit
headings.reviewNote: Requires 200+ subscribers for $250,000+ insurance, cash annual net premium in trust, certifications, and $5,000 security deposit.

headings.title: Security deposit as corporate insurance asset
headings.reviewNote: Deposited five thousand dollars constitutes part of insurance fund and corporate asset.

headings.title: Trust deposit held for protection of policyholders
headings.reviewNote: Securities held in trust by director for benefit, protection, and security of policyholders and beneficiaries.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; 200-subscriber/$250,000 threshold, $5,000 security deposit asset status, and policyholder trust verified.

headings.title: Application and published notice of business relinquishment
headings.reviewNote: Company president and secretary apply under oath; director publishes notice twice in Jefferson City newspaper.

headings.title: Surrender of deposited securities upon satisfaction of liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Director delivers deposited securities to company upon proof that all debts and liabilities are paid or provided for.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939 note, and § 375.480 cross-reference; relinquishment notice in state capitol newspaper and securities surrender verified.

headings.title: Minimum mortuary premium calculation and expense loading
headings.reviewNote: Requires mortuary premium at least equal to yearly term based on actuaries' table at 4 percent, plus age-based loading.

headings.title: Authorized premium payment schedules in advance
headings.reviewNote: Premiums payable annually, semiannually, quarterly, bimonthly, or monthly in advance.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939 note, and 1954 Old Reliable Soc. v. Leggett annotation; 4% combined experience minimum mortuary premium, loading, and payment schedules verified.

headings.title: Insurance fund composition and emergency fund reserve
headings.reviewNote: Mortuary premiums, loadings, and interest constitute insurance fund; excess held as emergency fund and may be deposited with department.

headings.title: Extra premium assessment upon emergency fund exhaustion
headings.reviewNote: If emergency fund exhausted, director requires officers to notify policyholders to pay extra equitable premium within thirty days.

headings.title: Proportionate policy commutation for nonpayment of extra premium
headings.reviewNote: Failure to pay extra premium within thirty days results in proportionate commutation of policy liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939 note, and 1954 Old Reliable Soc. annotation; insurance/emergency fund, 30-day extra premium call on exhaustion, and proportionate commutation verified.

headings.title: Issuance of limited payment and investment policies
headings.reviewNote: Companies may issue limited payment or investment policies with actuarially increased net term premiums improved at 4 percent.

headings.title: Separate reserve fund and deposit for paid-up policies
headings.reviewNote: Premium increases reserved in separate fund to sustain policies after premium cessation; deposited with department.

headings.title: Statutory valuation upon failure to specify reserve portion
headings.reviewNote: Failure to state sustaining portion in policy triggers valuation under combined experience table at four percent.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939 note, and 1954/1968 case annotations; tightened subsection 2 title; limited payment policy reserves, deposit, and 4% valuation verified.

headings.title: Policy specification of payment sums and contingencies
headings.reviewNote: Policies must specify sums promised and payment times upon contingency; company obligated absent fraud, breach, or commutation.

headings.title: Suspension of policy issuance upon unpaid final judgment
headings.reviewNote: Refusal to pay claim for ninety days after final judgment triggers director notice prohibiting issuance of new policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; policy payment specification and suspension of new policies after 90-day unpaid final judgment verified.

headings.title: Medical examination requirement and eligible beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Applicant must be examined by appointed physician; beneficiaries limited to spouse, representative, relative, heir, creditor, or insurable interest.

headings.title: Beneficiary change and wife's consent for creditor substitution
headings.reviewNote: Beneficiary changeable under bylaws; change from wife to creditor requires her written consent.

headings.title: Insurable interest of qualified charitable organizations
headings.reviewNote: Section 501(c)(3) entities have insurable interest upon designation, gift, or written consent under section 376.531.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and history (1939–1997); tightened subsection 2 title; medical exam, eligible beneficiaries, wife's written consent for creditor change, and 501(c)(3) insurable interest verified.

headings.title: Prohibition of premium and dividend discrimination
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits discrimination between policyholders of same class and life expectancy regarding premiums, returns, or dividends.

headings.title: Requirement that policy express entire insurance contract
headings.reviewNote: Agent cannot make insurance agreement other than as plainly expressed in issued policy.

headings.title: Director referral of policy violations to attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Director reports discriminatory or improper policies to attorney general, who demands compliance within thirty days.

headings.title: Attorney general injunction proceedings for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Attorney general institutes restraining proceedings if company or agent fails to comply with demand.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1939 note, and §§ 376.500/376.510 cross-reference; discrimination ban, entire-contract rule, and attorney general 30-day demand/injunction verified.

headings.title: Foreign company emergency reserve and investment standards
headings.reviewNote: Foreign company must prove emergency reserve equal to Missouri requirement, held for policyholders and invested per home state law.

headings.title: Foreign company net premium standard and premium tax
headings.reviewNote: Foreign company must collect net premiums in advance and pay annual one percent tax on Missouri gross premiums in lieu of other taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; tightened subsection 2 title; foreign company emergency reserve, net premium standard, and 1% Missouri gross premium tax verified.

headings.title: Board reincorporation under regular life insurance law
headings.reviewNote: Board may accept chapter 376, amend articles with attorney general approval, file with secretary of state and director, and deposit securities.

headings.title: Powers and privileges of reincorporated regular life company
headings.reviewNote: Reincorporated company exercises all legal rights and privileges of companies originally incorporated under chapter 376.

headings.title: Continuation of existing contracts and pending legal actions
headings.reviewNote: Reincorporation does not modify existing contracts or liabilities, nor prejudice pending legal actions or acquired rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1939 note; tightened subsection 1 title; stipulated premium reincorporation under §§ 376.010–376.670 and contract/action continuity verified.
